excerpts.title: Placing shot boundaries
excerpts.why: A cut is placed midway between the last sample of one shot and the first of the next, the only unbiased estimate the grid allows.
text: // segmentsOf splits samples into runs and fills in plan.Segments, which is every
// step both the stepped and the tracked proposal share.
// Shared rather than copied because the boundary rule below is the one thing a
// tracked run must NOT do differently: a track that placed its cuts half a sample
// later than the stepped path would disagree with the tool's own advisory output
"no subject was detected in any sampled frame; there is nothing to propose. "+
"Author reframe.anchors by hand, or check that the source decodes")
// A boundary is placed MIDWAY between the last sample of one run and the first
// sample of the next, not on the first sample of the next.
// The sampler sees the shot change only at the first frame that already belongs
// to the new shot, so all the grid can say is that the cut happened somewhere in
// the gap between those two samples. Taking the later endpoint asserts the latest
// moment consistent with the evidence, which is wrong by up to a full sample
// interval and wrong in one direction every time: the outgoing shot's framing is
// held over the head of the incoming one. The midpoint is the only unbiased
// estimate available, and it halves the worst case to 1/(2*SampleRate).
// This became visible on 2026-08-03 when the sampler stopped mislabelling its own
// frames. `fps` had put content half a sample later than SampleTime claimed, and
// subtracting that half-interval from every boundary cancelled this bias by
// accident — two errors that hid each other. Measured against the advert's
// hand-authored, eye-verified boundaries, the midpoint is closer than either
// 38.105 -> 38.25, all inside 0.15 s where the uncorrected grid was out by as
// The first anchor is moved to 0. A segment's samples begin at the first frame
// where the subject was actually seen, which can be a fraction of a second in;
// leaving the anchor there would let the manifest's base anchor frame the
// opening frames, which is exactly the class of bug that shipped an ad opening
